title: Roundness, Completeness and Nested-Ball Fixed Points in Revised Fuzzy Metric Spaces
content: Revised fuzzy metrics express separation through continuous triangular conorms and induce metrizable topologies with open and closed balls. We formulate fuzzy-metric roundness in the revised language and prove that the closure of every open revised fuzzy ball is contained in the corresponding closed ball. A two-point counterexample shows that equality can fail, correcting an overly general ball-closure assertion in the literature. We characterize nonroundness by attainment of a positive minimum by a radial map on an open set not containing its centre, and show that the standard revised fuzzy metric induced by a metric is round exactly when the original metric is round. We obtain factorwise characterizations of roundness for finite maximum products and of both roundness and completeness for countable weighted maximum products. We also prove that every nontrivial revised fuzzy metric admits a topologically equivalent nonround truncation. After establishing the separation-based Cantor characterization of completeness, we derive local fixed-point principles from decreasing families of invariant round balls with vanishing revised fuzzy diameter. Unlike algebraic contraction theorems, these principles require no prescribed global contractive inequality. A nonlinear example shows that the method applies to a self-map that is not a Banach contraction on the relevant invariant domain.
